title: Tick-borne encephalitis vaccine
what: A vaccine shot that protects against tick-borne encephalitis, a viral infection of the brain carried by ticks. It is a course of several shots.
why: For people who live in or visit forests and nature in places where tick-borne encephalitis occurs.
duration: the shot takes a few seconds; with the check-up usually 15 to 40 minutes; the course is usually 3 shots, then boosters
tell_doctor: If you are sick now or have a fever
Allergies, especially to egg protein, and reactions to past vaccines
When you plan to go to the forest. There are faster schedules

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: The vaccine is given when you are healthy. You will be examined before the shot.

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: It is best to start the course early, usually in winter or early spring. Ask your doctor.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes so the shoulder is easy to uncover.

steps: A doctor or nurse asks how you feel and takes your temperature
The skin is wiped and the shot is given
The vaccine is recorded in the documents
After the shot, sit at the clinic for about 30 minutes
feel: Sometimes the spot aches for 1 to 2 days
Sometimes headache, weakness or a mild fever
after: Stay near the office for 30 minutes
It is better to go to the forest no earlier than 2 weeks after the second shot. Ask your doctor
Boosters are usually every few years. You will be told the date
red_flags: Trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, a rash all over: call your local emergency number

faq.q: Does the vaccine protect against all tick-borne diseases?
faq.a: No, only encephalitis. Check yourself after being in the woods and use tick repellents.

faq.q: What should I do if a tick bites me?
faq.a: Carefully remove it whole, or go to an urgent care clinic. Tell your doctor about the bite.

reminders.text: Tick-borne encephalitis vaccine tomorrow. Bring your vaccination record.
